findings.reason: the measured 241 dispositions and 959 git calls come from un-narrowed call sites, not from missing machinery, so the plan should state the endpoint as every caller narrowing and the brief must name the owner to extend.
findings.text: §2's endpoint (the scope check costs what the candidate node's paths can meet) is already implemented and already wired on both admission paths (`reckon/crew/dispatching/preparation.py:762` and `reckon/crew/dispatching/launch.py:897` pass `candidate_paths`/`candidate_repositories`), and the only exhaustive read left on the preview path is the `report_live_conflicts` call at `reckon/crew/dispatch_plan.py:1119`, which passes no candidates; the same un-narrowed read recurs at `reckon/crew/dispatch_claims.py:2097` (`_racing_claim_current`, inside the racing wait) while `reckon/crew/dispatch_claims.py:2580` already shows the narrowed call shape

findings.reason: the section reads as a new caching layer when the injection point exists, and the plan should state that the sibling call sites keep the same one-listing contract or that one pass holds one listing.
findings.text: §3's one-listing-per-pass already has both halves: `_resolved_reviewed_run_id` accepts a shared `pointers=` argument (`reckon/crew/recovery_review_delivery.py:231`) that `_pending_requests` does not supply, so `_reviewed_run_id` resolves each review request with its own listing; the same un-shared listing recurs at `reckon/crew/recovery_review_dispatch.py:1007`, `reckon/crew/recovery_review_dispatch.py:3025`, `reckon/crew/recovery_review_dispatch.py:3612`, `reckon/crew/recovery_review_dispatch.py:3930`, `reckon/crew/promotion_scope.py:645` and `reckon/crew/promotion_scope.py:872`

findings.reason: the refresh should adopt the snapshot's currency and staleness rules, so its no-input-read and pending-with-age tests measure an existing owner rather than a second one.
findings.text: §4's two behaviours are already owned: `pointer_is_current` (`reckon/crew/station_store.py:793`) exists so an unchanged pointer is not re-read, and `reckon/roadmap_snapshot.py` owns a key over the store's write counter and the project's live runs, with the recorded rule that a stale record is answered from and marked stale rather than reported slow; a refresh that invents its own pending state beside it creates a second staleness rule for one project's answer

findings.reason: a 0/1 build count can be met by a private cache that diverges on invalidation, and the plan's own equality clause requires the snapshot key, so the section must be written to it.
findings.text: §5's build no roadmap / at most one / never reuse across a change is exactly the key `reckon/roadmap_snapshot.py` documents (plan state, HEAD, the store write counter, live runs, the composing code), and the write path at `reckon/mcp_edit_plan.py:1487` recomposes ahead of that owner; the change is to route the write's two returned fields through the snapshot, not to add build counting beside it

findings.reason: the plan should state the endpoint as the plan-keyed query over the store's own query keys and archive tables, so the worker extends `reckon/run_store.py` rather than building a parallel index the archive path will drift from.
findings.text: §6's plan-scoped read already has its owner and its indexes: `_RUNS_INDEXES` is generated from `QUERY_KEYS` (`reckon/run_store.py:80-83`) and the archive carries `archive.idx_runs_project` and `archive.idx_runs_node` (`reckon/run_store.py:988-991`), so visiting the whole of 11,360 rows to return 196 describes a query shape, not a missing index; a side index or payload-scan limit added in §6 would be a second owner of one query contract across the hot store and its archive

findings.reason: the plan already describes the same endpoint (stage times summing to the pass within 5 %), so this changes the brief's reuse map rather than the plan's record.
findings.text: §7 asks for receipts that name each stage with its time, but `_record_stage_timings` already writes `release_seconds`, `waits_seconds`, `launch_seconds` and `land_seconds` per pass and already takes the wait stage from its own clock; what is genuinely missing is the reads inside each stage, so a second receipt family for the same pass is a duplicate of the owner

findings.reason: without the per-read attribution on the existing verdict row, §9's ten live receipts reconcile against two records for one pass.
findings.text: §7's receipt is a thin layer over `_record_stage_timings` and gives no reason that recorder cannot carry the per-read split itself; the same shape recurs where §3 and §4 each would wrap `list_live` and `pointer_is_current` without saying why they cannot be extended

findings.reason: the section must account for its added surface in its own text, and adopting the snapshot's existing stale-not-slow answer would retire §4's addition.
findings.text: public_definitions 2875, cli_options 515, mcp_views 15, refusal_families 25; §4 adds a new `pending` answer state carrying an age to the refresh surface and §7 adds new receipt fields, and neither section names a state or field it retires or merges, or why nothing can be

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the seven endpoints concentrate in four existing owners (`reckon/crew/dispatch_claims.py`, `reckon/roadmap_snapshot.py`, `reckon/run_store.py`, `reckon/crew/admission/service.py`); no new module is needed to hide the behaviour each section asks for.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — every section's read-shape change has an existing owner, and the design otherwise re-implements keyed reuse (`reckon/roadmap_snapshot.py`), pointer currency (`reckon/crew/station_store.py`) and query indexing (`reckon/run_store.py`) rather than extending them.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 2875, cli_options 515, mcp_views 15, refusal_families 25; §4 adds a `pending` answer state with an age and §7 adds new receipt fields while neither section names what it retires or merges, or why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the machinery §2 asks for already exists and is reachable by extension: `_repository_scope_claims(candidate_paths=..., candidate_repositories=...)` in `reckon/crew/dispatch_claims.py:427` with the `relevant` gate at `:515` that costs no git at all for a pointer that can meet none of the candidate's roots.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §7 proposes a per-read timing receipt beside `_record_stage_timings`, which already records release/waits/launch/land seconds for every pass, so the added layer lacks a reason the existing recorder cannot be extended.
